body:
defaultConfigPath honors an absolute ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_CONFIG or XDG_CONFIG_HOME and ignores relative values. An absolute path can still resolve to a location inside the repository under review (for example $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/adv-config.json in CI), so repository content can supply model pins and cache entries through such a path or through a symlink that resolves into the tree.

Reproduction: set ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_CONFIG to an absolute path inside a repository that commits that file with a cache entry; the tool loads it during auto-detection.

Change: canonicalize the resolved config path (resolving symlinks on the existing prefix) and ignore any target contained within the working-tree/repository root, falling back to the home/XDG default. Keep the default home/XDG behavior unchanged.

Subprocess test harnesses currently isolate config via ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_CONFIG placed inside the throwaway repo dir; under this change those would be rejected, so move the isolated config to a temporary directory OUTSIDE the throwaway repo dir.

Acceptance criteria:
- AC1: an absolute config path inside the working tree is not loaded (falls back to the default).
- AC2: a config outside the tree (home/XDG, or an unrelated absolute directory) loads normally.
- AC3: a symlink whose target is inside the tree is rejected.
- AC4: subprocess test harnesses isolate config outside the repo dir; full suite green.

Related: T22 (CLI path containment). Some harness test files (test/loop-summary.test.mjs, test/loop-providers.test.mjs) are T7 rails; coordinate edits accordingly.
title: Reject config paths contained within the reviewed working tree (repo-containment, not just absolute)
